cards.title: 30 guesses for a billion
cards.text: Binary search halves the remaining range at every step, so finding an item among a billion sorted ones takes at most about 30 comparisons (2³⁰ ≈ 1.07 billion).

cards.title: Quicksort's bad day
cards.text: Quicksort averages O(n log n), but consistently bad pivots (say, always the first element of already-sorted data) push it to O(n²). Randomised or median-of-three pivots make that very unlikely.

cards.title: Hash tables aren't magic
cards.text: Hash tables give O(1) lookups on average, but if many keys collide in the same bucket, a lookup can degrade to O(n). Good hash functions and resizing keep collisions rare.

cards.question: Which data structure is Last-In, First-Out?
cards.explanation: Think of a stack of plates: you take the last one you put on top.

cards.statement: Merge sort is a stable sort: equal elements keep their original order.
cards.explanation: Standard merge sort is stable because, on ties, it takes from the left half first.

cards.statement: Inserting at the front of an array is as fast as inserting at the front of a linked list.
cards.explanation: A linked list inserts at the head in O(1); an array must shift every element along, which is O(n).
